OWN-004.title: Feature flip: fixed small t — t ≤ 3 is trivially universal on odd n, fixed t = 4 has a primality-type failure set
OWN-004.connection: The word tuv − u − v with u = 1 gives (t−1)v − 1, so t = 2 or 3 (and t = 1, = Frobenius numbers g(u,v) = uv−u−v, e.g. g(2,n+2) = n) represents every odd n trivially. Fixed t = 4 gives n = 4uv − u − v ⟺ 4n+1 = (4u−1)(4v−1), which fails e.g. whenever 4n+1 is prime. ES needs the union over t ∈ 4ℤ (plus the glued third generator u+v in the semigroup picture).
OWN-004.why: Shows precisely which features (t restricted to 4ℤ, union over levels) turn a trivial or primality-type single-level statement into a plausible universality statement.
OWN-004.first_step: Tabulate which odd n (and primes) fail to be 4Cuv − u − v for each fixed C = 1,2,3,… separately (each level has its own divisor-type failure set) and for unions over C ≤ K.

OWN-023.connection: Heath-Brown (Quart. J. Math. 37 (1986)): among any three multiplicatively independent candidates, at least one is a primitive root for infinitely many p (so at most two are exceptional). Squares can never be primitive roots (F08-like obstruction). Shares F08w, F22 (Chen/Fouvry–Iwaniec sieve).

OWN-038.connection: A ∀p-in-a-class existence theorem proved by explicit construction: primes p ≡ 5, 7 mod 8 are congruent numbers, and 2p is congruent for p ≡ 3, 7 mod 8 (Heegner points / Monsky's mock Heegner points). Shares F01p, F29 (residue class of p matters).

OWN-042.connection: m/n = (m−4)·(1/n) + 4/n, so ES gives m − 1 terms (with repeats). Flip: m/n in m − 2 terms is Sierpiński's 5/n problem for m = 5 (3 terms); for general m it trivially fails at small n (e.g. n = 1), and whether it holds for all large n is to be checked (for fixed 3 terms, Schinzel exceptions grow like exp(m^{1/3+o(1)}), Pomerance–Weingartner). F11, F12.

OWN-048.connection: 8/n has genuine exceptions (11, 17, 131, 241 among primes > 3; recomputed by brute force for p < 400) while satisfying the same local/BM features (needs check). Any ES argument must visibly use a property false for 8.

OWN-056.connection: ES fixes the linear part to 4/n; rationality of the Soddy curvature additionally needs (x+y+z)/(xyz) to be a rational square. Links ES to Apollonian-type curvature questions (F08 via HKRS).

OWN-078.connection: Solved universal unit-fraction statement under a parity restriction; ES fixed-length with no parity constraint. Note: for odd n, 4/n with all three denominators odd is impossible (4xyz is even but n(xy+yz+zx) is odd), so ES at odd n always uses an even denominator.

OWN-102.title: Hardy–Littlewood Conjecture H (large non-square n = p + k²) / Bateman–Horn: singular series with Legendre-symbol factors
OWN-102.connection: Representation counts whose singular series involve (n/ℓ) — e.g. HL Conjecture H, where squares n are excluded (n − k² factors). ES's main term M_BM has the same Legendre-symbol structure and also degenerates at squares (F20, F08).
